Andersen says most of her services are second relationships, but some are firsts and come from “tech-challenged women. I call them Paypals because I really only want to work with an Ivy League grad. And with a Paypal, I don’t care if they’re liberal or conservative, if they’re religious or judgmental. But they three things have to be really clicking. We talk on a lot of different levels. We talk deep and we have dinner dates. I ask it’s not about money or success. It’s whether they’re able to be kind.
Andersen honestly reports that many clients have experienced multiple breakups with other Bay Area individuals. Similar to many successful people in their late thirties, Andersen has experienced significant personal success in finding love. She met her husband on Nantucket at a wrestling competition where a luxury cruise ship to Antarctica was their prize. Yet, wedding days, years, and careers do not always end in romantic resolutions: Andersen and her husband divorced eight years later.
Andersen says that some of her male clients have gone through three divorces already. She emphasizes that her service is much more focused on long-term success than just providing hookups. But it's a plus if you're the "love concierge." Andersen says. She can evaluate potential suitors a few times before suggesting someone new. Similar to any traditional matchmaker, Andersen evaluates her candidates for marital history, children, political views, and work history, especially in large tech companies.
Clients sign initial nine-month contracts and can reside anywhere within Silicon Valley's 452 square miles to qualify (the Hill Bar at the Rosewood hosts parties in Woodside, which is part of San Mateo County). “When you’re working for CEOs, they’re going to understand that any company spending $50,000 is very, very serious about it,” Andersen says.
